the proinflammatory cytokine IL-1 increases the activity of fibroblast-expresses peptidases, thus reducing the bio-availability, and the immunogenicity, of the tumor antigen gp100(280–288).
IL-1 increases the activity of fibroblast-exposed enzymes and this effect is accompanied by an increase in the amount of peptic by-products and a reduction of the bioavailability of the epitope.

the use of adjuvants inducing proinflammatory cytokine expression may increase the activity of peptylases expressed by fibroblastic cells, thus, reducing the bio-availability and effectiveness of the peptides used for immunotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role played by the cytokine IL-1 on antigen processing.
the possible effect of proinflammatory mediators on the activity of fibroblast-ex-pressed peptidases, and with the possible use of these mediators as adjuvants.
the study of the possible effects of proinflammatory factors on the activity of peptic enzymes, and the possible use of these factors as adjuvants in the development of peptide-based vaccines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of IL- 1 on fibroblasts may be relevant for the design of vaccines based on peptides.
IL-1, and other pro-inflammatory cytokines, may be considered as adjuvant-like molecules, able to modulate the effectiveness and the specificity of peptide-based vaccines.

IL-1 may have a dual effect on the bio-availability and immunogenicity of peptides, since on one hand, it may enhance the activity of proteases, and on the other hand it may increase the expression of antigen-presenting molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-1, by increasing the activity of proteolytic enzymes, reduces the bio-availability and immunogenicity of peptides used as tumor vaccines.
IL-1 is able to induce an increased activity of fibroblast-expressing enzymes, with an increased production of peptidase by-products.
, in addition to the known effect of adjuvants on antigen-presenting cells, they can also influence the activity of bystander cells, which can be important for the outcome of vaccination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of adjuvants that increase the activity of peptic enzymes may reduce the bioavailability of peptides used as antigens in vaccination.
the use of proinflammatory adjuvants should be avoided in peptide immunotherapy.
, in order to improve the effectiveness of peptides, the use of adjuvants able to modulate the activity of pepta-lytic enzymes expressed by bystander cell types should be considered.
